entries.title: Smirnov's local-to-global metrization theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on 3-colourings of planar graphs. (1) Kostochka and Yancey's theorem, the case k = 4 of Ore's 1967 conjecture on the minimum number of edges of k-critical graphs: every finite 4-critical graph G satisfies 3|E(G)| ≥ 5|V(G)| - 2, by their potential method. (2) Grötzsch's theorem: every finite triangle-free planar graph is 3-colourable, deduced from (1) as in Kostochka–Yancey, with the topological crossing argument replaced by a K5-minor argument with an apex inside a face. (3) Aksenov's and Jensen–Thomassen's theorem: a triangle-free planar graph plus one edge is 3-colourable (Borodin–Kostochka–Lidický–Yancey, Theorem 2). (4) A triangle-free planar graph plus one vertex of degree at most 4 is 3-colourable (BKLY, Theorem 4). (5) The Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem: every finite planar graph with at most three triangles is 3-colourable, following BKLY's short proof (Theorem 7), with precolouring extension for 4- and 5-cycles (BKLY Theorem 5, for arbitrary cycles) and a combinatorial region (Jordan-type) theorem for rotation systems making the interiors and outer faces of the paper precise. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks on this definition K4 is shown planar and K5 and K3,3 non-planar.
entries.title: Grötzsch's theorem, Ore's conjecture for k = 4 (Kostochka–Yancey) and the Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem

entries.abstract: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability theorem is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every *proper common MCS prefix* (the sets the constructive proof actually visits -- a hypothesis strictly weaker than the every-subset bound), the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering. This strengthening (exists_common_ordering_prefix) makes the matching result a genuine corollary; the every-subset version exists_common_ordering is retained as a special case.
entries.title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance

entries.abstract: For every Borel probability law on the real line that is symmetric about zero and satisfies 0 < a <= |X| <= b almost surely, the support ratio b/a <= sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) guarantees E exp(t X) <= exp(t^2 E X^2 / 2) for every real t. The inequality is strict for nonzero t, and the actual variance is the optimal quadratic proxy. An explicit symmetric law on {-R,-1,1,R} violates the bound near zero for each larger ratio R. In the normalization 3-sqrt(6) <= X^2 <= 3+sqrt(6), the development also establishes the sharp eighth-order MGF gap with its optimal interiority coefficient, identifies the unique law with Gaussian fourth-moment contact, and proves the sharp global Wasserstein bound for the squared law at every feasible fourth-cumulant deficit, including attainment. The proof combines a convex endpoint reduction, control of the entire moment tail, exact rational Bernstein certificates, and an explicit affine transport coupling.
entries.title: Sharp universal support criterion for sub-Gaussian laws

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of exponential separation for analytic iterated function systems on the real line. Strong exponential separation holds on an open and dense subset in the C2 topology and follows from an explicit criterion involving dual projections. The development characterises conjugacy to self-similar systems and proves dimension consequences conditional on cited results of Rapaport and Bowen, including a drop in the L^q dimensions of the natural measure of a concrete three-map example.
entries.title: Exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line: Lean formalisation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the flatness half of the main theorem of the OpenAI preprint "The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers" (September 24, 2026): for 1 ≤ d ≤ 6, every nonnegative, nonzero, one-homogeneous global minimizer u of the one-phase Bernoulli energy J(v; B) = ∫_B |∇v|² + 1_{v > 0} in ℝᵈ is flat, that is, u(x) = max(⟪x, e⟫, 0) for almost every x, for some unit vector e. The minimizer class is the one of Alt and Caffarelli, written out from Mathlib definitions: on every ball B, u ∈ H¹(B) and J(u; B) ≤ J(v; B) for every v ∈ H¹(B) with v − u ∈ H¹₀(B), with weak gradients and H¹₀(B) (the closure of C_c^∞(B)) defined in the statement itself. The proof follows the preprint's universal-certificate method; the classical regularity theory of one-phase minimizers that the preprint cites is proved, in this repository or its dependencies, and the classification in dimensions d ≤ 4, which the preprint cites, is proved by the same exclusion method with new certificates.
entries.title: Flatness of one-homogeneous one-phase Bernoulli minimizers in dimensions at most six

entries.abstract: Theorem C: for finitely many distinct points a of the unit sphere of R^d and any L in O(1,d) (L^T S L = S with S = diag(-1, 1, ..., 1)), the configuration a is Euclidean Ramsey if and only if its image under the Möbius map phi_L is Euclidean Ramsey. There is no affine-spanning hypothesis. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). Corollaries, also proved: every Möbius image of a finite set of distinct unit-sphere points with real algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; and for distinct rationals t_i and arbitrary reals k != 0 and c, the circle points circ(k t_i) and circ(t_i + c) form Ramsey sets, where circ is the stereographic chart of the unit circle. The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math fd4aeeb2, result 172), whose 28 files are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. The Lorentz matrix transports OpenAI's real tensor criterion; OpenAI's descent and sufficiency conclude. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
entries.title: Möbius invariance of the Ramsey property for finite spherical sets

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of A quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions: for every number field K, its Dedekind zeta function has no zeros in Re(s) > 31/32. The formal statement asserts the existence of a holomorphic function away from 1 that agrees with Mathlib's Dedekind zeta function for Re(s) > 1 and is nonzero for Re(s) > 31/32 with s different from 1. The corollary gives the same zero-free bound for Hecke L-functions associated with finite-order Hecke characters, including s = 1 for nonprincipal characters. These characters are represented in Lean as ray class characters. This repository contains the substantive Lean development, including its Challenge and Solution.
entries.title: A uniform zero-free region for Dedekind zeta functions

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the classical existence of finite triangle-free graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number. For each integer k at least two, it constructs a finite simple graph whose clique number is exactly two and whose chromatic number is exactly k. The proof iterates the Mycielski construction from the complete graph on two vertices. This is the Tutte–Zykov variant recorded with Erdős problem 627, not a solution of that problem's open asymptotic limit question.
entries.title: Triangle-free graphs with prescribed chromatic number

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the counterexamples of Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin (arXiv:2610.03229) to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo on heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics. n agents with real opinions and positive bounds r_1, ..., r_n update synchronously, x(t+1) = A(x(t)) x(t), where row i of A(y) averages uniformly over the neighbourhood N_i(y): the j with |y_i - y_j| <= r_i in the SBC model (synchronized bounded confidence) and <= r_j in the SBI model (synchronized bounded influence). Conjecture 2.2 says the proximity digraph is constant after a finite time; Conjecture 2.3 says every trajectory reaches a fixed state or is eventually pseudo-stable (the agents split into two non-empty classes, fixed at their limits or moving strictly towards them from one side); Theorem 6.4(iv) says a trajectory whose digraph is constant from some time on is eventually pseudo-stable. For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.
entries.title: Heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics: counterexamples to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 resolution of both parts of Erdős problem 836 (posed by Erdős and Shelah; Erdős and Lovász, 1975) on 3-chromatic intersecting r-uniform hypergraphs, together with structural bounds on the Erdős–Shelah codimension-one avoidance question. For Part (i), it formalizes Noga Alon's equitable-partition construction with (2r - 2) + C(2r - 2, r - 1) / 2 active vertices to disprove the O(r²) vertex bound for all r ≥ 2. For Part (ii), it adapts and generalizes Liam Price's minimal-blue bipartite double-counting argument to prove the universal bound r ≤ 2t + 1 when distinct edges meet in at most t vertices, establishing that every 3-chromatic intersecting r-uniform hypergraph has two distinct edges meeting in at least r/3 vertices, that linear intersecting hypergraphs are 2-colourable for r ≥ 4, and that avoiding pairwise intersection r - 1 forces minimum degree ≥ 3, degree ≥ 4 on multi-intersections, and |E(H)|, |V(H)| ≥ 9 at r = 4.
entries.title: Erdős 836: vertex counts and pairwise edge intersections in 3-chromatic intersecting uniform hypergraphs

entries.abstract: For every natural n at least 68000, the formalization constructs n injectively indexed points in the fixed Euclidean space R^458999. Distances between distinct points are at least one, distances attached to different unordered non-diagonal pairs differ by at least one, and both every pair distance and the diameter are strictly below (37/50)n^2. The dimension and threshold are explicit sufficient bounds; no optimality or independent priority review is claimed. This code-only port preserves the theorem of the cited public formalization. The full migrated build and final axiom audit have passed; the hosted sandboxed Comparator check has also passed.
entries.title: Fixed-dimensional separated Euclidean distances below 0.74 n squared

entries.abstract: Let (Ω, μ) be a measure space and a = (a_k) a family of m square-integrable functions whose Gram matrix ∫ a a* dμ is the identity. Then for every n ≥ m there are points x₁, …, xₙ ∈ Ω and weights w₁, …, wₙ > 0 with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑ᵢ wᵢ a(xᵢ) a(xᵢ)* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I in the Loewner order. For the counting measure on a finite set Ω this is the theorem for finitely many vectors: if v_k ∈ ℂᵐ, k ∈ Ω, satisfy ∑_k v_k v_k* = I, then for every n ≥ m there are weights s_k ≥ 0, at most n of them nonzero, with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑_k s_k v_k v_k* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I, so a reweighted subset of at most n of the vectors is a spectral sparsifier of their sum. The original theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava has the constants (1 ∓ √(m/n))²; with m − 1 in place of m, following Chkifa, Dolbeault, Krieg and Ullrich, the statements here are slightly stronger.
entries.title: The sparsification theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava

entries.abstract: A regular Hausdorff space is metrizable if and only if it has an open basis expressed as a countable union of locally finite families. Every layer can have arbitrary cardinality. The development proves the necessity using metric paracompactness, perfect normality from the basis, continuity of arbitrary locally finite bounded coordinates, and a compatible metric via a countable product of metric function spaces. It assumes neither second countability nor separability and includes empty spaces. This formalizes classical mathematics, without claiming new mathematics or first formalization priority.

entries.abstract: For every finite simple r-uniform hypergraph F with r >= 3 and m >= 1 edges, the Turán density is at most 1-c_r/m^((r-1)/r), where c_r=(1/(4r^2))(4/r)^(1/r)(1-1/r)^(2-2/r). The formalization proves the finite embedding argument using two potentials and the Lovász Local Lemma, constructs the extremal numbers, and proves the existence of their binomial-normalized limit by vertex deletion and double counting.
entries.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turán densities

entries.abstract:
The main theorem (thm:A, Theorem A "Every dimension", of version 1) of the manuscript "Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension", in one statement. For every dimension s >= 3, every integer base q >= 2 all of whose prime factors are at least s - 1, and every k >= 1, the explicit digital net P^{U*_s}_{k,q} over Z/qZ with N = q^(sk) points (Definition def:Ns for the places infinity, 0, 1, ..., s-2 -- the Faure-Hammersley frame in graph form with the gauges of prop:Ns and prop:Gs -- and the design U*_s of Definition def:Ustar, whose columns are short vectors of the lattices of admissible columns, chosen level by level by Babai rounding) (1) is a (0,sk,s)-net in base q, so every cell of side q^(-k) holds exactly one point, and every point of [0,1]^s lies within Euclidean distance sqrt(s) N^(-1/s) of a net point (covering radius); (2) if q >= 5 a*_s + 4, any two distinct net points have toroidal and Euclidean distance at least (1 - a*_s/q) N^(-1/s), for every k >= 1, and for k >= 2 and q > (s-1) a*_s some two distinct points are closer than (1 - a*_s/q + (s-1)(a*_s+1)^2/q^2) N^(-1/s) (first-order sharpness of a*_s). The constant a*_s = max_c sum_{d != c} max_j |E_{d,j}[c]| of def:Ustar satisfies a*_3 = 2 and, for s >= 4, a*_s <= 2(s-1)^(3/2) (3/2)^(s-2) (s-2)!, and this explicit bound is e^(s log s + O(s)) (|log(bound) - s log s| <= 3s). So a*_s <= e^(s log s + O(s)), an upper bound only. Matching bounds of the same order N^(-1/s) for arbitrary N-point sets (the volume argument behind "optimal order") are classical and not formalized.
Comparator configuration: comparatorHeadline.json (4 compared theorems, all proved, no sorry): Z3NetA.theoremA, and three theorems showing inside the entry that the data the definitions introduce by choice are the paper's -- Z3NetA.ustarCols_spec (the columns E_{d,j} of def:Ustar exist and are unique), Z3NetA.gamma_spec (gamma_j of lem:sat(ii) exists and is unique) and Z3NetA.net_wellDefined (the reduction R_S -> Z/qZ, a solution U' of the residual problem and the coefficients beta of prop:Gs exist, and the net built from any of them is the entry's net). The Challenge (Headline/Challenge.lean) imports only Mathlib and contains verbatim copies of the 43 definitions of the proof side (Z3Net/FDefs.lean, Z3Net/ThmADefs.lean) that the statement reaches. The Solution (Headline/Solution.lean) obtains the theorem from Z3NetA.thmA of the full formalization in the same Lake project (whose single configuration comparator.json covers all compared theorems of the statement library).
entries.title: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension

entries.abstract: Every exact bilinear algorithm for multiplying two 3 × 3 matrices over an arbitrary field uses at least 21 products of input linear forms. The theorem includes finite and infinite fields in every characteristic. The input linear forms and output matrices are unrestricted. This is a lower bound for exact bilinear complexity, not for border rank or general arithmetic circuits. The repository contains the proof development and an interface stated entirely with ordinary Mathlib matrices and linear maps.
entries.title: A lower bound of 21 for 3 × 3 matrix multiplication over every field

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem (1970), conjectured by Erdős in 1964: every finite graph with maximum degree at most r has an equitable proper colouring with r + 1 colours, i.e. a proper colouring whose colour classes differ in size by at most one. The exact form is also proved: if the number of vertices is s(r + 1), every colour class has exactly s vertices (the colouring form of Erdős Problem #914). The proof follows the short argument of Kierstead and Kostochka (2008): induction on the number of edges; after deleting an edge, a nearly equitable colouring is repaired by moving vertices along paths of an auxiliary digraph on the colour classes (Lemma 2.1); when the large class is inaccessible, a family of terminal classes, solo edges and a discharging count with weights q/|S_z| (Lemmas 2.2–2.3) produce a recolouring that either finishes the colouring or strictly increases the number of accessible classes, using the induction hypothesis on the inaccessible part. The general case is reduced to the divisible one by adding a disjoint complete graph.
entries.title: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colourings

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of both parts of Erdős problem 1105 on the anti-Ramsey number AR(n, H), the maximum number of colors in a surjective edge-coloring of K_n with no rainbow copy of H. Part (i) proves the Erdős–Simonovits–Sós (1975) cycle formula AR(n, C_k) = ((k - 2) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) n + O(1) for every fixed k ≥ 3 (Montellano-Ballesteros and Neumann-Lara 2005; Choi 2011), together with the exact triangle value AR(n, C_3) = n - 1 and the explicit two-sided bounds ⌊n / (k - 1)⌋(choose(k - 1, 2) + 1) - 1 ≤ AR(n, C_k) ≤ ((k - 2) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) n - 1 for all n ≥ k ≥ 3 via private-color deletion and weak anticyclic block decompositions. Part (ii) proves the Simonovits–Sós (1984) and Yuan (2021) exact path formula AR(n, P_k) = max(choose(k - 2, 2) + 1, choose(ℓ - 1, 2) + (ℓ - 1)(n - ℓ + 1) + ε) for all n ≥ k ≥ 5, where ℓ = ⌊(k - 1) / 2⌋ and ε = 1 for odd k and 2 for even k, via representative-graph exchanges, finite host-window reduction, degree-core elimination, and 2-connected circumference bounds.
entries.title: Erdős 1105: anti-Ramsey numbers for cycles and paths

entries.abstract: A continuous closed surjection from a Hausdorff space, with compact fibres, preserves and reflects ordinary open-cover paracompactness. The paracompact image is proved Hausdorff without assuming target separation. Supporting selected results give inverse transfer without separation or surjectivity, forward transfer to a regular target, local finiteness of images of arbitrary indexed families, and the regular-space criterion using arbitrary locally finite refinements. No metrizability, countability, local compactness or uniform fibre-size assumption is imposed. The source is based on Munkres section 41 exercise 8 and Sakai Theorem 2.6.3(a),(e); it does not claim new mathematics.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Perfect surjections and paracompactness

entries.abstract:
The ambidextrous moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a connected planar shape that can be moved, from one starting position, around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width that turns right, and also around the corner of a hallway that turns left. Dan Romik (Experimental Mathematics, 2018) constructed a shape of area M = 1 + 4Y^2 + arctan Y = 1.64495..., where Y = 0.2980... is the positive root of 4Y^3 + 3Y = 1, and proposed it as a likely solution; in 2025 Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner listed the problem as open.

This entry proves that Romik's ambidextrous sofa is optimal and that it is the only optimal shape. Every compact connected set that continuous rigid motions, starting in the same orientation, move through both hallways has area at most M, with equality if and only if the set is the image of Romik's sofa by a rotation and a translation. It also proves that Romik's sofa and its images by rotations and translations move through both hallways, that its area is M, that its convex hull is the convex body given by its support function, and that M is Romik's closed form (3 + 2 sqrt 2)^(1/3) + (3 - 2 sqrt 2)^(1/3) - 1 + arctan(((sqrt 2 + 1)^(1/3) - (sqrt 2 - 1)^(1/3))/2).

The proof splits the convex hull of a sofa into two caps, one for each hallway, and bounds the area of the sofa by the sum of their scores. The score of each cap is at most M/2, with equality only for Romik's cap, and when the area is M the sofa is recovered from its caps. Two steps use Jineon Baek's theorem that Gerver's sofa is optimal for the ordinary moving sofa problem (arXiv:2411.19826); its Lean formalization comes from lean4-moving-sofa and is included in the repository.
entries.title: Optimality and uniqueness of Romik's ambidextrous sofa, formalized in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Expected Syzygies and Fröberg’s Conjecture through Degree 2d: assuming the Expected Syzygy Conjecture over a characteristic-zero field, general degree-d forms have the positively truncated Hilbert function predicted by Fröberg’s conjecture in every degree through 2d. The implication holds for every positive number of variables and degree and every number of generators, with one common nonempty open set for all the stated degrees.
entries.title: Expected syzygies and Fröberg’s conjecture through degree 2d

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the optimal universal 1 -> 2 cloning of a qubit, with every figure of merit finite: a channel from one qubit to two is a finite Kraus family K_i : C^2 -> C^2 (x) C^2 with sum K_i^* K_i = 1 (the blank qubit is fixed, so this is a 1 -> 2 map; the Choi-Kraus theorem is not proved), the two clone fidelities of a pure input psi are Re <psi| Tr_2 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi> and Re <psi| Tr_1 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi>, and F1-bar, F2-bar are their averages over the six Pauli eigenstates (1 +- sigma)/2, Gaussian-rational density matrices (the six states form a 2-design, the octahedron being a spherical 3-design, so these equal the Bloch-sphere averages of Gisin-Massar, as Bowdrey-Oi-Short-Banaszek-Jones 2002, (11), print for qubit maps; that equality is neither used nor claimed). Theorems, kernel-only: for every channel (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 <= 5/6, so some unit psi has min(F1, F2) <= 5/6 (Gisin-Massar 1997, their largest-eigenvalue bound; Bruss-DiVincenzo-Ekert-Fuchs-Macchiavello-Smolin 1998 within the symmetric isotropic ansatz), proved by a six-term sum of squares in the Kraus entries; the Buzek-Hillery channel (1/6) V1 rho V1^* + (2/3) V2 rho V2^* (V1|0> = 2|00>, V1|1> = |01> + |10>, V2|0> = (|01> + |10>)/2, V2|1> = |11>; Buzek-Hillery 1996, (3.29)) is a channel whose two marginals are rho -> (2/3) rho + (1/6) Tr(rho) 1 (their (4.6); Werner 1998, (3.7)-(3.8)), so F1 = F2 = 5/6 for every unit psi (their root fidelity sqrt(5/6), p. 7); a channel with (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 = 5/6, or with F1, F2 >= 5/6 on every unit psi, is the Buzek-Hillery channel as a map (the uniqueness under the average-fidelity criterion is proved here from the certificate; Keyl-Werner 1999 prove uniqueness under the worst-case one-clone criterion Delta_one and Werner 1998 under the global criterion; the Kraus family and the dilation are not unique, Roubert-Braun 2008), so 5/6 is the greatest t for which some channel has t <= F1(psi), F2(psi) for every unit psi, in Lean's IsGreatest form; F1-bar, F2-bar >= 1/3 for every channel, attained for the first clone by the universal NOT on it with a maximally mixed second clone (the universal-NOT bound of Buzek-Hillery-Werner 1999 and Gisin-Popescu 1999, in six-state average form); the asymmetric trade-off a b <= a(a + 2b)(1 - F1-bar) + b(2a + b)(1 - F2-bar) for every channel and all weights a, b >= 0, also with worst-case fidelities in place of the averages (the largest-eigenvalue bound of Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf 2005, Section II, in every dimension, with their conic alpha^2 + alpha beta + beta^2 = 1 written homogeneously; Hashagen 2017, (6.4a); the curve of Niu-Griffiths 1998, (6.29); the conic of Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.31), and x^2 + x'^2 + x x' >= 1/4 of Cerf, PRL 2000, (6); Buzek-Hillery-Bednik 1998, (11); the full achievable region in Hashagen 2017 and Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021), proved by a sum of squares polynomial in a, b; the family (A0 rho A0^* + A1 rho A1^*)/(2(a^2 + ab + b^2)) with A0|0> = (a + b)|00>, A0|1> = a|10> + b|01>, A1|0> = a|01> + b|10>, A1|1> = (a + b)|11> (the optimal asymmetric cloner of Niu-Griffiths (4.13), Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.28), Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf (19), Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005 (27)) consists of channels with marginals rho -> (1 - b^2/s) rho + (b^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1 and rho -> (1 - a^2/s) rho + (a^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1, s = a^2 + ab + b^2, so F1 = 1 - b^2/2s and F2 = 1 - a^2/2s on every unit psi, with equality in the bound at the weights (a, b), and for a, b > 0 equality holds only for that channel (proved here; Hashagen's uniqueness is within symmetrized channels); a = b is the Buzek-Hillery channel; hence the square-root form sqrt((1 - F1-bar)(1 - F2-bar)) >= F1-bar + F2-bar - 3/2 (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (23)), its worst-case form, and equality along the family for a, b >= 0 (the curve of Niu-Griffiths (6.29)). For every channel 3(F1-bar + F2-bar) - 7/2 <= sqrt((3F1-bar - 1)(3F2-bar - 1)), binding also where a clone is below 1/2 (with the floor, the necessity half of Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021, Theorem 6, at d = 2 for the six-state averages; Hashagen 2017, Theorem 6.4, in entanglement fidelity), proved by a Gram identity in the Kraus entries and Cauchy-Schwarz, with equality along the family when (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0 and, with neither clone perfect, only there; a perfect clone on average leaves the other at 1/2 (Hashagen 2017, p. 20, via Nielsen 2002, (3)); the asymmetric bound holds for all real a, b with (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0, the family being its only equality case when the product is positive and a, b != 0, and at (3, -1) it is the anticloning bound 3F1-bar - 5F2-bar <= 1, attained only by asymChannel 3 (-1), at (13/14, 5/14); F2-bar = 1/3 forces F1-bar <= 5/6, and (5/6, 1/3) is attained only by asymChannel 2 (-1), on every unit psi, the Buzek-Hillery clone with its anti-clone (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (12)-(15)), and likewise with the clones exchanged; if (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 >= 5/6 - eps, the Kraus operators lie within total squared Frobenius distance 6 eps of span{V1, V2}, and ||Lambda(rho) - Lambda_BH(rho)||_F <= 200 sqrt(eps) ||rho||_F for every input rho. entries.abstract: A Lean proof that every family of 14-element subsets of a 24-element set covering all 4-element subsets has at least 20 members, so the covering number C(24,14,4) is at least 20, improving the previously tabulated lower bound of 19. Point derivation (the Schönheim bound) then gives C(25,15,5) >= 34, improving the tabulated 32. The proof excludes a hypothetical 19-block covering: a sum-of-squares identity for the minimum-degree incidence vectors forces balanced components, a rigidity theorem for eleven-block (22,12,3) covers controls suitable completions and derivatives, and two counting contradictions finish the argument. The Lean proof follows the accompanying paper, paper/c24-14-4.pdf.
entries.title: Lower bounds for the covering numbers C(24,14,4) and C(25,15,5)

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.1 of Hilbert Functions of Chopped Ideals of General Plane Points over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields: the full Hilbert function of degree-d chopped point ideals, the regular-sequence cases, the least stabilization degree, and the Expected Syzygy Conjecture.
entries.title: Hilbert functions of chopped ideals of general plane points

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three papers of J. Fröhlich and T. Spencer (Communications in Mathematical Physics, 1981, 1982 and 1983), with the two-dimensional multiscale analysis in the finite-volume form of V. Kharash and R. Peled (2017). For the two-dimensional plane rotator it proves the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition: the two-point function decays exponentially at high temperature, while at low temperature it obeys the power-law lower bound of Theorem C and still tends to zero, so that there is no long-range order. The same multiscale expansion in charge ensembles gives the absence of screening and the power-law decay of fractional charges in two-dimensional Coulomb gases (Theorems A and B), the phase diagram of the Z_n clock models with an intermediate massless phase (Theorem 7.1), disorder bounds for the Villain model (Theorem D) and the roughening transition of the solid-on-solid model (Theorem 7.3), as well as the four finite-square theorems of Kharash and Peled. For the four-dimensional Villain U(1) lattice gauge theory at large beta it proves that the integer-valued dual gauge field has the exponential moments of a free massless field up to a renormalization of the coupling from beta to beta''(beta) with beta''/beta -> 1, in finite volume (2.93) and for every limit state along cubes; that a translation-invariant limit state has a field-strength correlation that is not summable, obtained as the limit of the finite-volume field-strength correlations, which is the paper's massless photon; the perimeter law of the Wilson loop at large beta and its area law at small beta; a perimeter law for the disorder operator of the Z_N gauge theories; and long-range order of the Villain XY model in every dimension D >= 3. For the Anderson tight-binding model on Z^nu at large disorder, or at high energy with Gaussian disorder, it proves exponential decay of the Green function with polynomially high probability, uniformly in the imaginary part of the energy (Theorem 1.2), its almost-sure decay, and the vanishing of the Kubo diffusion coefficient wherever the density of states is positive (Theorem 1.1). The FS82 statements are in finite volume or about limit points along cubes; the thermodynamic limits that the paper takes from Ginibre's inequalities are not formalized. Corrections to the printed texts are listed in the README.
entries.title: Classical theorems of Fröhlich and Spencer: the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition, massless phases of abelian gauge theories, and Anderson localization

entries.abstract: Exact final-gradient bounds for convex functions with Lipschitz gradient on real Hilbert spaces, under an initial-distance bound, for every horizon and nonnegative constant step. The factor is the maximum of reciprocal linear progress and the quadratic oscillation power, with genuine smooth convex attaining examples. The formalization includes the joint progress potential, complete sampled equality trajectories in both strict branches and at balance, and a direct transfer from actual constrained proximal minimizers to sharp residual and terminal objective-residual bounds. All ten principal declarations are listed in comparator.json; VERIFICATION.md records checks.
entries.title: Sharp last-iterate bounds and extremal trajectories for constant-step gradient descent

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 1180 and its quantitative variants on representing every residue modulo a prime p as a sum of at most C(ε) modular inverses n⁻¹ (mod p) with 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε and gcd(n, p) = 1. Formalizing Glibichuk's 8-fold bilinear covering theorem via additive energy and Cauchy–Davenport together with an inductive asymmetric two-block prime-reciprocal construction, this development proves the affirmative existence theorem for all ε > 0 and all primes p, the discrete large-prime bound C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8(⌊1/ε⌋ + 1)² = (8 + o(1))ε⁻² (and ≤ 32ε⁻² uniformly on (0, 1]), the asymmetric staircase bounds C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k(k + 1) whenever (2k + 1)ε > 2 and C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k whenever (2k - 1)ε > k (giving C_asymp(ε) ≤ 16 for ε > 2/3 and ≤ 24 for ε > 3/5), and Shparlinski's O(ε⁻³) bound. It also proves the large-prime pigeonhole lower bound 1/ε ≤ ⌈1/ε⌉ ≤ C_asymp(ε), the small-prime exponential lower bound 2^(1/ε) ≤ 4 C(ε), the strict separation C_asymp(1/n) < C(1/n) for all n ≥ 15, and the disproof of the unthresholded all-primes optimality statement.
entries.title: Erdős 1180: representing residues as sums of modular inverses with small denominators

entries.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization proves that, for every integer n at least two, the direct product of the free group of rank n with the infinite cyclic group has a positive cone generated by finitely many elements as a semigroup if and only if n is even. It formalizes Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of Hang Lu Su's arXiv:2608.31103v1. The even-rank construction passes a positive cone through two finite-index subgroups. The converse derives the parity obstruction from finite circle domains and their endpoint actions. The required base-cone theorem and the supporting algebraic and dynamical arguments are proved within Lean.
entries.title: Finitely generated positive cones in F_n × Z

entries.abstract: Formalization of Dowker (1951), Theorem 4: normality plus ordinary countable paracompactness of an arbitrary topological space X is equivalent to normality of X times the closed unit interval, and to strict continuous insertion between arbitrary real upper and lower semicontinuous functions h<g. No T1 or Hausdorff assumption on X, boundedness or uniform gap is added. Companion compact metrizable product theorem (Lemma 3) and countable-cover/decreasing-closed-sequence equivalences (Theorem 2) are included.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Dowker's countable paracompactness, product normality and strict insertion characterization

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of the spherical Gaussian spin-glass dynamics and its positive-semidefinite Cugliandolo--Kurchan limit, including the physical variational response, entropy and Fisher estimates, stationary translated clusters, general-spin selection and aging bounds, and stationary relaxation. Theorem 11.4 covers every integer p >= 3 and beta > 0. The cubic product inequality includes beta = beta_d; strictly positive Fisher-cost conclusions require beta > beta_d. The root Challenge retains the original complete-conclusions theorem with the five principal theorem groups and all-spin forward theorem, sharing CK, stationary-profile, dimension-subsequence, density and Fisher-majorant witnesses. The same file separately retains the original Proposition 5.7 statement for every CK solution, every late sequence and every raw translated cluster.
entries.title: Aging in Spherical Spin Glass Dynamics

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.
entries.title: Generalized Markoff strong approximation

entries.abstract: For every natural number k, the series whose nth term is the sum of the kth powers of the positive divisors of n, divided by n factorial, is irrational. This gives the positive-exponent statement of Erdős problem 252 and also includes exponent zero. The proof combines factorial-tail integrality, a finite coprime dilation grid with exact finite-difference cancellation, and incompatible progression means obtained by a fresh-prime refinement. It has no prime-pattern conjecture or unproved number-theoretic hypothesis. The Lean development also proves convergence and the equivalence of its natural-index series with the series starting at one.
entries.title: Erdős 252: irrationality of the factorial divisor-sum series

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the conditional lower bound for the number h(x) of pairs of coprime positive integers a < b < x with equal sums of divisors. Assuming Hypothesis A⁺, which supplies sufficiently many primes p with smooth p+1, h(x) exceeds x^(2-ε) for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large natural x. The argument adapts Pollack and Pomerance's finite counting method. A⁺ itself, the squarefree strengthening, and the accompanying paper's argument relying on the WD preprint are not formalized here.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #824 under a smooth shifted-prime hypothesis

entries.abstract: Quantitative permanence and recovery bounds are established for mass-action systems with vanishing reverse rates. For a finite weakly reversible network with rates proportional to powers of epsilon, eventual concentration bounds depend on the spread of the rate exponents, with geometric constants chosen before the individual rates. For an explicit three-species network, a prepared region admits global positive solutions with three distinct concentration scales. Every prepared solution reaches and remains in a smaller target by time (31/10)/(p^2 h^7), while an explicit prepared solution cannot enter before 400/(1313 p^2 h^7). Inventory inequalities give additional necessary restoration and depletion times from arbitrary positive initial states. A continuous reverse-exponent family retains arbitrary admitted prefactors and yields matching worst-case prepared recovery orders, together with exact common-clock transport, preparation identities and cumulative reverse-reaction bounds. Abstract constant-capacity and open-range state-dependent inventory comparisons are included without assuming monotone inventories.
entries.title: Quantitative permanence and recovery with vanishing reverse rates

entries.abstract: Exact worst squared spectral gaps for finite open chiral chains with inhomogeneous strong-bond lower bounds and weak-bond ratio intervals. The scalar optimum is the minimum over the ordered one-switch endpoint configurations, with a two-certificate reduction when cuts are allowed. Strictly positive weak lower bounds give a complete point-or-edge classification of scalar minimizers and an exact aligned-channel equality criterion for arbitrary complex matrix disorder. The sharp channel bound includes the finite chiral Hamiltonian spectral bridge.
entries.title: Exact robust gaps in finite open chiral chains

entries.abstract: For every positive generating degree d, there is a variable threshold depending only on d such that, over every infinite field and for every number of general degree-d generators, the quotient polynomial ring has Fröberg's predicted Hilbert function through degree 2d. The threshold is independent of both the field and the number of generators. The prediction uses positive truncation at the first nonpositive coefficient of (1-t^d)^r/(1-t)^n. The development includes a direct construction for d at least three and a separate quadratic argument in arbitrary characteristic.
entries.title: Fröberg's conjecture through degree 2d in sufficiently many variables

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "Prime-power structure of the stable regime for modular Schur numbers" (docs/paper/modular-schur.pdf in this repository). The modular Schur number S_m(k,ℓ), introduced by Chappelon, Revuelta Marchena and Sanz Domínguez (2013), is the largest N such that 1, …, N can be coloured with k colours so that no colour class contains a solution of x_1 + ⋯ + x_ℓ ≡ y (mod m). For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1). The main theorem is the closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for every k ≥ n − 1. D'orville, Sim, Wong and Ho (Integers 25 (2025) #A62) gave it when gcd(m,ℓ−1) = 1 (their Corollary 5). The general case is a short corollary of the singleton criterion and their Corollary 3; to the author's knowledge it is first stated in the paper. The proof turns on one value: ℓ copies of n sum to n modulo m, so the class {n} alone breaks the rule, while each of 1, …, n − 1 is safe in a class of its own. The formalization also proves the one-colour closed form S_m(1,ℓ) = min(ℓ − 1, ⌊m/ℓ⌋) for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, which answers Problem 1.3 of D'orville et al.; the bound S_m(k,ℓ) ≤ m − 1 of Chappelon et al.; and the reduction from integers to residues modulo m. Twelve theorems with Mathlib-only statements are compared by lake comparator (statement identity, permitted axioms, and replay through the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels); their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 33 project modules also contain further results, listed in LEAN_STATUS.md, that are proved and axiom-audited but are not compared, among them the bound m/p, with p the least prime factor of m, on the size of a set of residues whose pairwise differences all lie in a proper subgroup of ℤ/m. An earlier computational part of the project, which uses native_decide, is not in this repository and is not part of these results. The informal proofs, the Lean formalization and the paper were produced with AI systems (Claude, Aristotle and GPT-5) under the direction of the author.
entries.title: Modular Schur numbers: S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for k ≥ n − 1, where n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1)

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of open phases with every prescribed finite replica symmetry breaking depth in mixed even-spin Ising models at zero external field and positive temperature. The first selected result constructs strictly increasing even degrees beginning at four and a nonempty open set of positive effective covariance coefficients, with an optimizing probability measure having exactly k+1 support points. The independent statement uses concrete Gaussian Cole–Hopf recursions and comparison against all finite schemes at every competing depth. The substantive development constructs minimizers over all probability measures and includes the revised quadratic-inclusive universal transition, exact phase geometry and asymptotics, atomic Hessian, entropy, and analytic comparison results.
entries.title: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the solved parts, extremal bounds, and finite verification up to 10000 for Erdős problem 261 on representing n / 2^n as a finite sum ∑_{k=1}^t a_k / 2^(a_k) of distinct positive integers a_k. Proves the Borwein–Loring telescoping family n = 2^(m+1) - m - 2 (resolving Part (i) that infinitely many positive integers n admit such a representation), verifies every integer 1 ≤ n ≤ 10000 via a coalesced dyadic block certificate forest (Theorem 3.5 of Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadło 2020), constructs infinitely many rationals with at least 2^m distinct infinite representations for every m ∈ ℕ, and proves the Tengely–Ulas–Zygadło sharp extremal bound n ≤ 2^(t+1) - t - 2 and its equality uniqueness, first-term localization a_k ∈ [n+1, n+3], 2-adic last-gap divisibility 2^(a_{t+1} - a_t) ∣ a_{t+1}, the punctured-interval infinite family n_k = (2^(4k+2) + 1)/5 - 4k, and arbitrary-length splicing.
entries.title: Erdős 261: dyadic weighted representations n / 2^n = ∑ a_k / 2^(a_k)

entries.abstract: Machine-checked upper bound on Erdős problem 607. For n ≥ 2 let F(n) be the number of distinct multiplicity sets A(P) that can arise from a collection P of n points of the plane, where A(P) is the set of block sizes (point counts) of the lines determined by P. The proof shows that the lines of P form a pairwise-balanced design on the n points (every pair of points lies on exactly one line, and each line contains at least two points), so A(P) is exactly the set of block sizes of such a PBD. Hence F(n) is bounded by the number of PBD profile sets on n points, and the Colbourn–Phelps–Rödl (1984) Theorem 2.4 bound exp(c·√n) on that quantity gives F(n) ≤ exp(c·√n) for every n ≥ 2. The bound is stated for n ≥ 2 — the range where the bound is meaningful (a single point determines no line) — so the hypothesis is non-vacuous. The CPR-1984 PBD bound is a published theorem and is taken as the hypothesis hCPR; it is cited, not re-proved here. Together with the Szemerédi–Trotter (1983) lattice-grid lower bound F(n) ≥ exp(c'·√n) (also cited, not re-proved), the order of growth is F(n) = exp(Θ(√n)). This repository contains zero axioms and zero sorry in the proof development (the only sorry is the deliberate statement surface in Challenge.lean).
entries.title: Erdos607

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of a deterministic rational nested-interval construction defining a particular transcendental real x in (1/4,1/3). For this x, no strictly increasing infinite sequence of positive integer denominators is optimal among all distinct-denominator strict Egyptian underapproximations at every order from any finite starting order onward. The formalization includes the fully specified terminating construction, all prefix and polynomial enumerations, a total executable rational approximation function, and the error bound |x-q_n| <= 2^(-n-1) for every n >= 0. It also proves attainment of the best finite underapproximation values. The independent Palomar statement quantifies directly over all sequences and all competing positive increasing lists. This is a specific effective example; the measure-zero and prior existence results are not claimed as new.
entries.title: An explicit computable transcendental counterexample for Erdős Problem #206

entries.abstract: Formalization of Michael (1968), Theorems 1.2 and 1.3: arbitrary indexed products of biquotient continuous surjections are biquotient, without separation assumptions; for a Hausdorff target, biquotience is equivalent to quotientness of the product with every identity map and to the same property for paracompact test spaces. The cover definition, filter and ultrafilter bridges, and an actual Hausdorff paracompact counterexample topology on the underlying target set are proved. Reverse tests use the target universe; the forward implication is separately universe-polymorphic.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Michael's biquotient-map product and characterization theorems

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that the independence sequence of every finite forest is unimodal: the numbers of independent sets with 0, 1, 2, ... vertices weakly increase up to some index and weakly decrease after it. This is the statement listed as Erdős Problem 993; later sources attribute the question to a 1987 paper of Alavi, Malde, Schwenk and Erdős. The first claimed proof for all finite forests is by T. Zhang and W. Li (self-archived preprints, September 2026). This repository formalizes a second proof, by W. Li, K. Vallier and T. Zhang: it adapts the public arXiv:2610.07943v1 and follows version 2.15 of that manuscript, deposited with restricted access and under revision. The Lean proof is computer-assisted and in two parts (at most 24 vertices; at least 25). About 13,700 finite computations are evaluated by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, on the three standard axioms. AI systems produced and reviewed all of the Lean; no human has read the Lean proofs. No manuscript cited is peer reviewed. No priority and no first formalization is claimed.
entries.title: Unimodality of the independence sequence of a finite forest (Erdős Problem 993)

entries.abstract: We construct uniformly bounded orthonormal bases for homogeneous holomorphic polynomials on complex unit spheres. Fix d >= 2 and N >= 0, and put m = d-1 and L = N+d-1. For each multi-index alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_d) of nonnegative integers with sum N, define s_b(alpha) = b + alpha_1 + ... + alpha_b, 1 <= b <= m, and the normalized monomial M_alpha(z) = sqrt((N+d-1)! / ((d-1)! alpha_1! ... alpha_d!)) z_1^alpha_1 ... z_d^alpha_d. Let F be the normalized Fourier matrix, with entries F_(t,s) = L^(-1/2) exp(2 pi i t s/L), for 1 <= t,s <= L. For each increasing m-element subset T = {t_1,...,t_m} of {1,...,L}, define P_T(z) = sum_(|alpha|=N) det[F_(t_a,s_b(alpha))] exp(2 pi i sqrt(2) sum_r alpha_r^2) M_alpha(z), where the determinant is over 1 <= a,b <= m. These polynomials form an orthonormal basis with respect to surface measure of total mass one on the complex unit sphere. Their absolute values on the closed unit ball are bounded by a constant depending only on d, independently of N and T. The construction and proof are formalized in Lean.
entries.title: Explicit uniformly bounded bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every dimension

entries.abstract: Ordinary mass-action realizations are characterized for a finite family of two-species modules coupled through a shared resource and buffer. Every positive parameter vector admits a strongly connected realization of the same polynomial field. A complex-balanced realization at a prescribed positive state exists exactly when the state is stationary and two explicit local flux inequalities hold, even when arbitrary finite auxiliary complexes on the same species are allowed. An explicit endpoint sign test determines the untransported heterogeneous parameter locus, and the state criterion extends to directed transfers of both private species. A homogeneous specialization has the sharp sharing threshold v <= n/8, including equality. Global positive solutions and permanence uniform over compact sets of initial conditions are established. For d >= 1, the positive equilibrium is unique and is locally exponentially stable in the homogeneous family. Complex-balanced realizations yield global convergence, including with transport, and local exponential stability is established for the transported complex-balanced family. An exact example at d = 1/10 has three positive equilibria, two locally exponentially stable and one unstable.
entries.title: Realizations and dynamics of shared-resource mass-action systems

entries.abstract:
Let N(σ,T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with real part at least σ and imaginary part of absolute value at most T, counted with multiplicity. For every fixed σ ∈ [1/2,1] and every ε > 0, we prove N(σ,T) ≤ Cσ,ε T^(A(σ)(1−σ)+ε) for all T ≥ 2, where

| σ interval | A(σ) |
| --- | --- |
| [1/2,9/13] | 3/(2−σ) |
| (9/13,5/7] | 18/(7σ+3) |
| (5/7,3/4] | 9/4 |
| (3/4,1] | 3/(2σ) |

The maximum of this coefficient bound is 39/17, improving the coefficient 30/13 in the Guth–Maynard bound. We also prove the separate estimate N(σ,T) ≤ Cε T^((39/17)(1−σ)+ε) for every ε > 0, simultaneously for σ ∈ [1/2,1] and T ≥ 2, with a constant independent of σ and T. The improved large-values estimate and its zero-density consequences are formalized in Lean.
entries.title: Zero-density estimates from an improved large-values bound

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential" by Armstrong, Bou-Rabee and Kuusi: the subdiffusive scaling limit of a Brownian particle whose drift is the gradient of a log-correlated random potential (Theorem A, in its introduction form and in its precise quenched form), quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem uniformly in the infrared cutoff (Theorem B), and large-scale Hölder regularity with a Liouville theorem (Theorem C), together with the supporting coarse-graining, elliptic-regularity and Markov-process theory. The theorems hold for every random environment satisfying the paper's standing assumptions (a GMCModel). The development builds on Mathlib and on the public CoarseGraining and MarkovProcess libraries. The three headline theorems are independently checked by the comparator pairs under SubdiffusiveProcessAudit/.
entries.title: Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of A. Kupiainen, R. Rhodes and V. Vargas (Annals of Mathematics, 2020) that the three-point structure constants of Liouville conformal field theory on the Riemann sphere are given by the DOZZ formula of Dorn–Otto and Zamolodchikov–Zamolodchikov. The structure constants are defined probabilistically: for 0 < gamma < 2, cosmological constant mu > 0 and charges satisfying the extended Seiberg bounds, C_gamma(alpha_1, alpha_2, alpha_3) = 2 mu^(-s) gamma^(-1) Gamma(s) E[rho^(-s)], where rho integrates explicit power weights against the Gaussian multiplicative chaos of the Gaussian free field pinned on the equator. The formalization proves C_gamma = C_gamma^DOZZ, expressed through the Zamolodchikov function Upsilon_{gamma/2}, at every point of the domain where Gamma(s) is finite, and at every point including the poles for the unit-volume constant; and it proves that the probabilistic reflection coefficient, built from Brownian motion conditioned to stay negative and lateral chaos, equals R^DOZZ (Theorem 3.5). The theorems hold for every model of the field and chaos, and models are constructed. All prerequisites are proved: the construction, uniqueness and moment theory of Gaussian multiplicative chaos and the extended Seiberg bounds (David, Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2016); the BPZ equations for degenerate four-point functions and the classification of their real single-valued solutions by the Gauss hypergeometric function (Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2019); analytic continuation of correlation functions, tail estimates for multiplicative chaos, fusion asymptotics, the shift equations and the quotient argument. Errata found in the three papers, and the places where the Lean statements differ from them, are recorded in docs/ERRATA-AND-DEVIATIONS.md.
entries.title: Integrability of Liouville theory: the Kupiainen–Rhodes–Vargas proof of the DOZZ formula
